findings.summary: Write-scope porcelain collapse struck FIFTH time overall and SECOND time in evidence-curator.yml itself: enforcement executed `CHANGED=$(git status --porcelain | cut -c4-)`, got the bare untracked-directory entry 'evidence/' for what were actually ~105 valid nested writes under evidence/run-memory/, and grep -Ev '^evidence/run-memory/' classified them as out-of-scope. Sequence fully log-pinned: validate step printed no errors; enforce step printed exactly 'Evidence Curator wrote outside its durable memory scope: evidence/' then exit 1; persist step never ran. A known-bad gate destroyed a SECOND complete recovery execution because intermediate fixes (d8343e7 feedback loops, 1b41981 recovery isolation, b888f30 validator keys) each cured a different gate while the scope guard stayed unfixed for ~2h48m after strike #4 (run 32881219633).

The cleanup-incident recovery PROTOCOL itself is now proven repeatable end-to-end: second independent execution selected exactly 32880942022, parsed all 102 deletion lines, ran a Git recovery sweep (125 remote heads by name; lab/* state/docs/results/reports + .spider receipts; per-id git log --all --grep), wrote 105 artifacts, and passed BOTH its own validation and the hardened workflow validator (dual count keys born from the 32882090239 mismatch worked as intended). Session-side discoveries reconfirmed at second pass: repo-hygiene.yml on main had LOST the accepted-state id-grep protection layer the executed v1 still had (restored post-run by a09d036); protection greps never covered evidence/** or .spider/**; 4 of 5 deleted council runs keep UNKNOWN per-run loss.

Sequential-gate whack-a-mole pattern: three successive curator failures (scope guard -> validator key -> scope guard again) each cost a complete ~12-20 min session while each remediation commit fixed exactly ONE downstream gate. This run cleared every gate EXCEPT the last one before persistence. Suggests gate ordering review: any post-session gate that can hard-fail should either be fixed in the same change as the previous gate fix, or persistence should precede enforcement (write to staging ref, then gate).

Run economics: ~11m46s wall (checkout fetch-depth=0 of many-branch repo + OpenCode install + ~11m25s agent session on opencode/x-preview-f-free); produced 105 files of validated output worth ~34 min delay before durable re-creation plus duplicate compute when 9e7d3ef re-ran the equivalent work. Todo-snapshot progression lines visible at 18:38:33 / 18:44:19 / 18:47:38Z show roughly half the session spent on Git cross-checks before any file writes.

failure_signatures: 'Evidence Curator wrote outside its durable memory scope:' followed by exactly 'evidence/' then 'Process completed with exit code 1' — the bare-ancestor-directory fingerprint of the porcelain-collapse variant (distinct from the pre-staged-files variant of strikes #1-#3). Regression discriminator: a flagged path that is an ANCESTOR DIRECTORY of the allowed scope = false positive.

research_opportunities: Extend the 30fc94f expanded-detection pattern (diff + diff --cached + ls-files --others) to the remaining unfixed consumers verified live on main at distillation time: physics-loop.yml x3 (:116,:185,:322), graph-loop.yml x3 (:116,:185,:322), cto-council.yml :113, runtime-loop.yml (:139,:205), frontier-research.yml :320 — any lane/frontier session creating a wholly-new directory mid-cycle can strand a finished audit/director step identically.

Persist-before-enforce ordering (or isolated staging ref) for workflows whose agent sessions produce large validated outputs ahead of scope checks — would have made both curator strandings and council #8's validation death non-lossy.
Gate-batch discipline: when a post-success gate kills a session, audit ALL remaining gates in the same fix, not just the one that fired.
